gaps.text: In-line measurement of Temperature with temperature sensor (for example Pt100 or thermocouple)

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Level: one model per method first, then a fused model on joined spectra with block scaling so that neither method dominates. Both methods must look at the same spot through the combined ATR/Raman probe head and the two streams must be synchronised to a common time step, with its own calibration and diagnostics for each block. The fused model has to beat the best single method on held-out batches, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)
No supplied page covers viscosity as a measurand of fiber-optic spectroscopy.
No supplied page covers temperature measurement by fiber-optic spectroscopy.

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform O3 by supporting a low-level fusion step where MIR ATR and Raman variables are concatenated, but the assessment should still verify that the streams are synchronised and block-scaled.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review and does not specify the same resin, dark matrix, combined ATR/Raman probe head, or in-line process, so transfer to this batch requires testing.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E01 ¶31

items.finding: The review reports that in some cases instrument complementarity alone was not sufficient to improve predictive performance for several CQAs, citing a Raman and FT-IR food study.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the gap's condition that a fused MIR ATR/Raman model must demonstrate improvement over the best single method on held-out batches before keeping the second instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study is on food analysis, not the customer's dark thickening resin or probe configuration, so it is a caution to test rather than proof of performance.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E01 ¶36
